newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso continues recovery, ends up vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso continues recovery, ends up vs dlr.

text.p: Colombia's peso continued to claw back ground lost against the dollar, rising 1.05 pesos to end at the session's 1,105.35 peak, interbank traders said.
"Banks bought dollars thinking the rate would rise. Then there was a sharp influx of greenbacks and banks were left with long positions," one dealer said.
Dealers said they expected large inflows of foreign capital at the end of this week and early next, which could push the peso up to 1,102 against the dollar.

Dealers said most of the foreign funds flowing into the market at present were destined to recapitalize financial institutions in the face of intense competition from Spanish banks extending their hold on the sector in Colombia.
Earlier this week, Spain's Santander Investment, a unit of Banco Santander completed its $141 million deal for a 55 percent stake in the former Bancoquia bank, now renamed Banco Santander Colombia.
The peso opened Thursday at 1,106.4 and sank to a low of 1,107.95 before closing at the high of 1,105.35. Dealers reported 450 trades worth a total $230 million.
